# Blocking socket calls that already held the GVL when
# TestEveryBlockingSocketCallReleasesTheGVL was written (2026-11-12).
#
# ⛔ THIS LIST MAY ONLY SHRINK. A new site not listed here fails the gate, and
# an entry that stops reporting fails it too — a stale allowance is a place the
# next regression hides.
#
# Why they matter: rbgo emulates a GVL, so a native call that blocks while
# holding it stops every other Ruby thread. A program that serves itself — a
# spec fixture, a test that binds a socket and connects to it, an embedder
# running a listener beside its own client — DEADLOCKS: the server thread
# returns from Accept and then parks on the lock the client is sitting on.
# Measured in ruby/spec as 39 of 56 library/net-ftp files killed by the clock
# and none under MRI (#916).
#
# Each line is file:line. Fix one by wrapping the call in ioBlock(vm, …) and
# deleting its line here. If the callers already release the GVL, mark the
# function //gvl:released-by-caller <reason> instead and delete the line.

# Net::FTP's DATA connection — FIXED and removed from this list, which is the
# only direction it may move. dialData, acceptData, sendData, retrlines and
# retrbinary all run their blocking call inside ftpIO now.
#
# acceptData was the one #916 is about: in ACTIVE mode the client listens and
# the server dials back, so a program that serves itself has both ends in one
# process and the Accept was parking every other Ruby thread — including the one
# that would have made the call it was waiting for.

# Net::IMAP: readLine/readLiteral are handed to imap.NewReader as callbacks and
# the binding has no ioBlock at all — the same shape Net::FTP had.
net_imap_bind.go:82
net_imap_bind.go:89

# Net::SMTP: the response reader.
net_smtp_bind.go:140

# Servers that accept connections from Ruby: an embedder running one of these
# beside its own client is the exact deadlock above.
httprb.go:148
hanami_bind.go:514

# ⛔ KNOWN GAP — three unwrapped conn WRITES this gate cannot see yet. They are
# COMMENTS, not entries: an entry that never reports is a failure by design, and
# these are invisible to the current rule. Written here so the gap is on the
# page rather than in somebody's memory.
#
#   socket_raw.go:206      s.conn.Write(msg)                  (still unwrapped)
#   net_ftp_bind.go        conn.Write in sendData             (FIXED: ftpIO)
#   nethttp_bind.go        conn.Write in nethttpProxyConnect  (covered by its
#                          caller's ioBlock)
#
# Why not gate on Write: adding it reported ELEVEN sites, eight of them not
# network writes at all — seven *bufio.Writer.Write (buffered; the socket write
# happens at Flush) and one bytes.Buffer in a file that does import net. The
# file-level rule that makes Read exact does NOT hold for Write; separating
# them needs the receiver's TYPE. Eight false alarms is how a gate gets
# switched off, so the rule stays narrow and the gap stays written down.
